newsitem.title: CANADA: Air Canada adds new Frankfurt, Seoul route.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada adds new Frankfurt, Seoul route.

text.p: Air Canada said it will launch new Calgary-Seoul and Montreal-Halifax-Frankfurt services this summer.
This is in addition to a previously announced Toronto-Osaka service which starts on July 1.
Air Canada will fly Calgary-Seoul weekly and Montreal-Halifax-Frankfurt twice weekly, starting in June.

The airline originally planned a daily Montreal-Frankfurt service which would stop twice weekly at Halifax and operate as a non-stop service the other five days. This was based on being able to operate Montreal flights from that city's Dorval Airport as opposed to Mirabel Airport.

In February, the shift of flights to Dorval, scheduled for June, was frozen by a court ruling. That ruling was overturned by a higher court two months later, but too late to enable the shift for this summer. The switch now is set for September 15.
After the February ruling, Air Canada said it would not operate Montreal-Frankfurt flights until 1998.
Market sources say there is strong demand for the cargo space for the Halifax-Frankfurt portion of the new service, particularly from seafood exporters.
Air Canada said Calgary-Seoul will be operated with an Airbus A340.
On the Toronto-Osaka route, the airline will not know until it has some experience with the route how much cargo it can carry from Toronto because of the need to load maximum fuel.
Eastbound from Osaka, the airline will have 19 tonnes of capacity per flight and no shortage of demand for it, an official told Reuters.
The airline said it would operate 10 flights a week between Vancouver and London and 11 between Vancouver and Frankfurt, up from seven a week in both cases last summer.

Between Toronto and London, Air Canada will operate up to five flights a day this summer, and it is planning to carry freight on all of them by expanding its US trucking. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
